title: Ethiopian Bread Pudding
community: Ethiopian households — the stale bread sweet
author: Mama Tigist
desc: Ethiopian Dabo Ferfar — stale Difo Dabo or Kita torn into pieces, soaked in eggs, honey, and cardamom-spiced milk, then baked. The Ethiopian zero-waste sweet — using stale celebration bread to create a spiced bread pudding.
longDesc: Dabo Ferfar is the Ethiopian cook's solution to stale celebration bread — the leftover Difo Dabo or Himbasha that has hardened is soaked in an egg-honey mixture and baked into a warm, fragrant pudding. Zero waste, complete deliciousness.
ingredients: 4 cups stale Ethiopian bread (Difo Dabo or Kita) — torn into pieces
1.5 cups milk (or plant milk for fasting)
steps: Beat eggs with milk, honey, cardamom, cinnamon, and salt.
Add torn bread pieces. Toss to coat.
Grease a baking dish with butter.
Pour bread mixture in. Press down gently.
Bake at 175°C for 20—25 minutes until golden on top and set.
Serve warm with a drizzle of honey.
chefTips: Stale bread works better than fresh — it absorbs the custard without becoming mushy.
Allow the full 15 minutes of soaking — the bread must hydrate completely.
cookingScience: Stale bread (partially retrogradated starch) absorbs the egg-milk custard more slowly and evenly than fresh bread — fresh bread absorbs so rapidly that it collapses into a paste. The retrogradated starch in stale bread maintains some structure during soaking, then softens as it bakes.
sustainabilityTips: The ultimate zero-waste use of stale celebration bread.
culturalNote: Ethiopian bread pudding is the final chapter of Ethiopian celebration bread — when the Difo Dabo of the wedding has gone stale, it becomes Dabo Ferfar, the family's next sweet. Nothing from a celebration is wasted.
